newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest -June 16.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest -June 16.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet and Brand-name Products.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - Accords over a reshuffle of the respective holdings between France's Publicis and U.S. True North, parent of Foote, Cone & Belding (FCB), were signed last week, Publicis chairman Maurice Levy tells the company's annual meeting. (Reuter)

PARIS - Two daughters of Publicis founder Marcel Bleustein-Blanchet give the Publicis annual meeting their views on a dispute over their stakes following the death of their father just over a year ago. Chairman Maurice Levy tells the annual meeting he expects Publicis to show double-digit profit growth for 1997. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET

PARIS - A poll by Ipsos for CB News and La Tribune shows many people working in France's broadcast industry support official measures being taken to prevent concentration of media ownership in limited hands. (La Tribune)

PARIS - Lagardere Group, faced with new links between Havas and Generale des Eaux and between Lyonnaise des Eaux and Bouygues, seeks ties with France Telecom for on-line services. Initially talks are likely to centre on bringing together Lagardere's Club Internet and France Telecom's Wanadoo service providers, but some Hachette executives want a broader alliance with France
Telecom. (Les Echos)
PARIS - France's public broadcasters, facing 1996 losses and difficulty balancing 1997 budgets, are looking to the new socialist government to ease the pressure on network finances.
(Variety)

PARIS - Jean-Marie Messier, chairman of France's Cie Generale des Eaux, rules out buying TF1, a rival to its indirectly-controlled pay TV unit Canal Plus in an interview with daily newspaper Liberation published on Friday. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - A novel package of advertising and sponsoring from French food group Danone is getting underway in France in the run-up to next year's World Cup football tournament, with the aim of tempting young football fans to taste Danone yoghurts and dairy deserts. (Reuter)

LONDON - LVMH Moet Hennessey Louis Vuitton says it requests arbitration from the International Chamber of Commerce over its dispute with Guinness Plc, relating to the proposed merger of Guinness with Grand Metropolitan Plc. (Reuter)
PARIS - French mattress maker Epeda cranks up innovation and advertising to awaken the bed market and persuade consumers to change beds more often. (Le Figaro)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
